Mūgĭōnĭa or Mūgōnĭa , ae, or Mūgĭōnis (Mucionis ), is, f. (porta),
I.a gate of ancient Rome, which was afterwards within the city: “in Palatio Mucionis a mugitu,” Varr. L. L. 5, § 164 Müll.: Mugionia porta Romae dicta est a Mugio quodam. Paul. ex Fest. p. 144 Müll.; Sol. 1, 24; cf. Becker's Antiq. 1, p. 109 sq.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
